title: Algorithms and online shopping
titleChinese: 算法对网购体验的影响
paragraphs: For many of us, online shopping has made the process of purchasing goods a far simpler and more fluid process. No longer do we have to head to the shops to browse and peruse various objects, wandering round endless aisles, before finally settling for the first thing we saw. These days, we find the item we want or need online, click on it, and check out its description and user reviews. If it fits the bill, we send it to our basket and pay. There seems to be a wealth of options at our fingertips. But how do we know the options that pop up in front of us really are the best deals. And how might algorithms help or hinder us?

Algorithms, simply put, are mathematical instructions which tell the computer how to solve problems. When shopping is involved, what is the problem they solve? Well, the algorithms instruct the computer which adverts to show and which products a user is most likely to splash the cash on. By analysing things we’ve previously bought or looked at, the algorithm can predict what goods we’re most likely to be enticed by. For some people, the idea of something guessing your preferences could sound a bit intimidating. But first, let’s look at the positives.

Time is an important thing – something we don’t want to waste too much of. By telling the computer to show us adverts for things we are interested in, it can save us a lot of time sifting through things or services that don’t match our criteria. They can also help us find the best deals.

However, there are some people who have concerns about the impact of algorithms on our shopping experience. It is possible that algorithms may only select options from a limited number of brands, or may favour products from certain companies. There are also concerns that we aren’t always shown the cheapest or best deal, even though that’s what we’re searching for. Finally, some algorithms generate ads which tell you there are only a limited number of items you’re interested in left. They might just be there to manipulate you.

So, the takeaway from this is that algorithms are here to stay, and it’s wise to know they exist. Whenever you’re shopping, be it online or off, make sure to shop around for the best deals. The first thing you see might not always be the best for you.

vocabulary.entry: online shopping 网购
vocabulary.example: Many people prefer online shopping for its convenience and lower prices.
vocabulary.translation: 很多人因为网购的便利和较低的价格而偏爱这种购物方式。

vocabulary.entry: fluid /ˈfluːɪd/ adj. 流畅的；顺畅的
vocabulary.example: The project requires a fluid process to adapt to changing needs.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目需要一套灵活顺畅的流程来适应不断变化的需求。

vocabulary.entry: browse /braʊz/ v. 浏览；随意翻看
vocabulary.example: I like to browse through fashion magazines in my free time.
vocabulary.translation: 我喜欢在空闲时间翻阅时尚杂志。

vocabulary.entry: peruse /pəˈruːz/ v. 仔细研读；详尽查看
vocabulary.example: She perused the menu for several minutes before ordering.
vocabulary.translation: 她仔细看了好几分钟菜单才下单。

vocabulary.translation: 一个小孩跑过货架通道，撞倒了一排陈列的瓶子。

vocabulary.entry: settle for 勉强接受
vocabulary.example: We had to settle for a smaller room as the hotel was fully booked.
vocabulary.translation: 酒店客满了，我们只好勉强接受一个小一点的房间。

vocabulary.entry: user review 用户评价
vocabulary.example: The user reviews of the camera were mostly positive.
vocabulary.translation: 这款相机的用户评价大多是正面的。

vocabulary.term: fit the bill 符合要求；满足需求
vocabulary.entry: fit the bill 符合要求；满足需求

vocabulary.translation: 我往购物车里加了几件商品，然后去结账了。

vocabulary.example: The museum has a wealth of ancient artifacts on display.
vocabulary.translation: 这家博物馆展出了大量的古代文物。

vocabulary.term: at our fingertips 触手可及；唾手可得
vocabulary.entry: at our fingertips 触手可及；唾手可得
vocabulary.example: With the internet, information is at our fingertips.
vocabulary.translation: 有了互联网，信息就唾手可得了。

vocabulary.term: pop up 突然出现；弹出
vocabulary.entry: pop up 突然出现；弹出
vocabulary.example: A notification popped up to remind me of the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 一条通知弹了出来，提醒我要开会了。

vocabulary.entry: algorithm /ˈælɡərɪðəm/ n. 算法
vocabulary.example: The app uses a complex algorithm to match users with suitable products.
vocabulary.translation: 这款应用使用复杂的算法为用户匹配合适的商品。

vocabulary.example: Bad weather hindered the progress of the construction work.
vocabulary.translation: 恶劣的天气阻碍了建筑工程的进展。

vocabulary.entry: instruction /ɪnˈstrʌkʃn/ n. 指令；指示

vocabulary.translation: 这个机器人会遵照设计者编写的指令运行。

vocabulary.term: splash the cash on 大手大脚地花钱买
vocabulary.entry: splash the cash on 大手大脚地花钱买
vocabulary.example: He splashed the cash on a new gaming console for his son's birthday.
vocabulary.translation: 他花大价钱给儿子买了一台新游戏机当生日礼物。

vocabulary.entry: analyse /ˈænəlaɪz/ v. 分析；解析

vocabulary.translation: 我们需要分析数据，找出问题所在。

vocabulary.entry: entice /ɪnˈtaɪs/ v. 引诱；吸引

vocabulary.translation: 这家公司用特价优惠吸引新客户。

vocabulary.entry: intimidating /ɪnˈtɪmɪdeɪtɪŋ/ adj. 令人胆怯的；令人不安的
vocabulary.example: The huge crowd at the concert was a bit intimidating for the young singer.

vocabulary.term: sift through 仔细筛选；逐一排查
vocabulary.entry: sift through 仔细筛选；逐一排查

vocabulary.translation: 她花了好几个小时来筛选所有的求职申请。

vocabulary.entry: criterion /kraɪˈtɪəriən/ n. （判断的）标准；准则
vocabulary.example: The main criterion for selecting candidates is their work experience.
vocabulary.translation: 选拔候选人的主要标准是他们的工作经验。

vocabulary.entry: favour /ˈfeɪvə(r)/ v. 偏袒；偏爱
vocabulary.example: The teacher does not favour any student in the class.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老师在班里不偏袒任何学生。

vocabulary.entry: manipulate /məˈnɪpjuleɪt/ v. 操控；操纵
vocabulary.example: He was accused of trying to manipulate public opinion.
vocabulary.translation: 他被指控试图操控公众舆论。

vocabulary.entry: takeaway /ˈteɪkəweɪ/ n. （事件的）启示；要点
vocabulary.example: The key takeaway from the lecture is the importance of lifelong learning.
vocabulary.translation: 这场讲座的核心启示是终身学习的重要性。

vocabulary.example: It's wise to shop around before buying a new laptop.
vocabulary.translation: 买新笔记本电脑前货比三家是明智的做法。

sentences.english: These days, we find the item we want or need online, click on it, and check out its description and user reviews.

sentences.chinese: 但我们怎么能确定，眼前跳出来的这些选项真的是最划算的交易呢？

sentences.chinese: 算法在这个过程中，又会起到帮助还是阻碍的作用呢？

sentences.english: Algorithms, simply put, are mathematical instructions which tell the computer how to solve problems.
sentences.chinese: 简单来说，算法就是一系列数学指令，它指导计算机如何解决问题。
